conviction_note: Ten small, sourced items that mostly offset: a priced 5.3% delivery beat with inventory run down and European demand recovering (+) against a priced 14% energy-storage miss, collapsing regulatory credits, China discounting and an energy-chief exit (-); the EPS bar was cut into the print (Zacks -3c/30d, JPM $0.49->$0.36), which helps a beat, but this name sold a revenue beat with an EPS miss -14.5% last print and 3 of its last 4 earnings reactions were negative, so p_up stays at 50 and the scaled move is 0 while the findings sum to +0.10; the reaction will be decided on the call (robotaxi/Optimus/capex), which nothing here can source.
bar: Revenue ~$27.8B (Zacks $27.8B, Visible Alpha via S&P Global $28.04B, Benzinga $27.62B, Hudson Labs $27.57B); adjusted EPS $0.44 (Zacks and Visible Alpha agree; Benzinga $0.41; JPMorgan $0.36); GAAP EPS $0.26 and gross margin 17.7% (Hudson Labs, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-preview-tsla-revenue-margins-outlook, 2026-10-05). Two agreeing sources on adjusted EPS, so not capped. The company-compiled earnings consensus on ir.tesla.com returned 403 and could not be read. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: deliveries +1.3% QoQ, storage flat QoQ, credits roughly flat against Q2's $28.24B, which puts revenue near $28.2-28.6B, about +1.5% over the ~$27.8B bar.
positioning_check: Short interest: the last figure found is 65.6M shares short at the 2026-03-31 settlement, days to cover 1.06, about 1.7% of 3.75B shares outstanding (https://equibles.com/stocks/tsla/shortinterest). It is stale but far from crowded. Skew is +1.57 vol points (25d put minus 25d call), mildly put-bid and labelled 'balanced'. Put/call open interest is 0.93. Event implied move is 5.3% (straddle 5.69%). Run-up is +5.5% over 5 days and +1.9% over 20 days; spot of 387.38 is up from the $362.44 close on 10-15 and the ~$371 after the 10-02 delivery beat, and 20.9% below the 52-week high. Retail-heavy holder base.

findings.finding: Q3 deliveries were 486,532, 5.3% above Tesla's own IR-compiled consensus of 461,974 (24 analysts) and above the Bloomberg 466k and Visible Alpha 469k figures. Production was 464,391, so roughly 22k units came out of inventory. That points to revenue at or slightly above the ~$27.8B bar, and to working capital helping FCF against a Hudson-cited consensus of about -$1.1B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +4.65% on the 10-02 delivery release (baseline). At the Q2 print on 2026-07-22, revenue beat ($28.24B against ~$25.7B) with deliveries 18% over consensus, but adjusted EPS missed ($0.33 against $0.51-0.55) and the stock fell -14.52% (baseline). A revenue beat has not paid on its own here.
findings.why_not_priced: The delivery count is fully priced (the stock rose 4.65% that day). What may not be is the revenue translation: the revenue consensus of $27.6-28.0B sits BELOW Q2's $28.24B, even though Q3 delivered more cars and slightly more storage. If the market had marked revenue up, the Visible Alpha and Zacks revenue numbers would sit above Q2, not below it.
findings.independence: Company release with production and deliveries (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-10-2-tesla-third-quarter-2026-production-deliveries-and-deployments). Teslanorth gives the same consensus (https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/02/tesla-q3-2026-deliveries/). These describe the same document, not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Energy storage deployments were 13.7 GWh, 13.8% below the 15.9 GWh consensus and only +1.5% QoQ against 13.5 GWh. That points to energy revenue below models. Partly offsetting, Q2 energy gross margin of 20.4% carried a ~$240M one-time vendor-cell warranty charge plus the loss of a >$200M Q1 tariff benefit, so energy margin should rebound in Q3 without that charge; the 17.7% consensus GM likely already assumes this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on storage alone. The energy margin swing from 39.5% to 20.4% was part of the Q2 miss that fell -14.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The deployment miss has been public since 10-02 and is largely priced. The margin direction is the open question: if the market expected a margin miss in energy, the GM consensus would not sit 90bp above Q2.
findings.independence: Q2 energy warranty and tariff detail is from the Q2 call coverage (https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/XBUL:TL0/transcripts/8973402, 2026-07-22). The miss and the deployment number share the delivery release with finding 1.

findings.finding: The WSJ reported on 2026-10-15 that Mike Snyder, VP of energy and charging and head of the Megapack business since Oct 2024, has stepped down, with AJ Booth succeeding him; Tesla has not commented. That leaves a leadership gap in the segment that is supposed to carry margin, in a quarter when deployments missed by 14%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in the baseline. The stock fell -1.29% on 10-15, the day the report circulated, with the Roadster event that evening.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the wire but has not been addressed by the company. The call is where it either gets explained away or gets attached to a weaker energy outlook. If the market were pricing it, energy-margin expectations would have been cut since 10-15; no evidence of that was found.
findings.independence: Stocktwits relays the WSJ report (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/tesla-energy-chief-mike-snyder-reportedly-exits-as-elon-musk-pushes-ai-and-robotics-pivot/cZxhOgzRBrZ). It is the same underlying report.

findings.finding: Regulatory credit revenue fell to $146M in Q2 2026 from $439M in Q2 2025 (-67%) and from ~$380M in Q1. The 10-Q adds new language: 'recent governmental and regulatory actions have restricted certain regulatory credit programs', and only $220M of credit RPO is due over the next 12 months. Credits are therefore stuck near $50-150M a quarter, at near-100% margin, against $400M+ a year ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The credit collapse was part of the Q2 margin miss (-14.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Q2 already reset the level. The residual is a y/y profit headwind of ~$300M that keeps the y/y EPS comparison ugly and a sub-1% credit contribution to margin. If any part of the bar still assumed a credit rebound, the consensus GM would sit above 17.7%.
findings.independence: Electrek ties the drop to CAFE penalties being zeroed out by statute (https://electrek.co/?p=476867).

findings.finding: China: CPCA September domestic retail was 64,837, down ~9% y/y and the fourth straight monthly decline; YTD domestic is down ~12% while exports doubled. Tesla is running October discounts of CNY 5,000 on Model 3 and CNY 7,000 on selected Model Y. That is a Q4 price-and-margin headwind the call has to address.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean line history. JPMorgan cited US and China weakness when cutting its Q3 delivery forecast in September.
findings.why_not_priced: Small discounts in one region get little attention next to a global delivery beat. If it were priced, the Q4 GM estimates would have been trimmed after the 10-02 beat; instead, consensus EPS fell for Q3 only. Sized net of Europe, which is growing (finding 6).
findings.independence: Drive Tesla Canada carries the same CPCA data (https://driveteslacanada.ca/?p=125285), so it is the same data set.

findings.finding: Forward demand outside China looks strong. EU+EFTA+UK registrations Jan-Aug were 191,787, +43.3% y/y (ACEA); September registrations rose 62% in France and 38% in Sweden. Autoevolution reports Tesla has largely run down its inventory, with delivery estimates for most models and markets now beyond January 2027. Tesla raised US Model Y upper-trim prices in May, and the Cybertruck Standard sold out for 2026. Pricing power should support the Q4 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Q2's stronger volume did not stop a -14.5% reaction on margins.
findings.why_not_priced: Wait times past January 2027 mean supply-constrained demand. That is a margin and Q4 delivery statement, not just a Q3 one. The previews focus on margin compression and capex; if backlog were priced, Q4 delivery and margin estimates would have risen after 10-02.
findings.independence: European registration data from Finviz (https://finviz.com/news/397487/tesla-registrations-rise-across-several-european-markets-in-september) is a different source from the autoevolution backlog claim. The Q2 call said production is supply-constrained on batteries and chips (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/TSLA-2Q26-AI-Summary).

findings.finding: Tesla held 11,509 BTC, with digital assets at $674M on 2026-06-30 (10-Q). Bitcoin rose ~43% in Q3 2026 (from ~$58.5k to ~$84k), so the fair-value gain is roughly $290M pre-tax, about $0.06-0.08 a share. Few EPS models include it. It is unclear whether Tesla's 2026 non-GAAP includes it: in 2026 the 'restructuring and other' line stayed at $0 despite a $334M H1 BTC loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 2025 an $80M BTC gain went largely unremarked in the reaction (+2.28% at that print).
findings.why_not_priced: A mark-to-market gain is rarely in consensus. If it were modelled, the adjusted EPS consensus would have risen as bitcoin rallied through Q3; instead it fell 3c in 30 days. It has no path to guidance, so it is sized as a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.
findings.independence: The Q3 bitcoin return is from CryptoBriefing (https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-jumps-q3-2026-outperforms-gold-stocks/), a different source.

findings.finding: Tesla holds ~19M SpaceX shares, valued at $3,007M on 2026-06-30 (~$158 a share), after a $1.005B Q2 gain that was excluded from non-GAAP. SPCX traded at $149.74 on 09-03 and ~$152 mid-September, so expect a small GAAP mark-to-market loss in Q3 (likely $0.1-0.3B, quarter-end price not found). It is excluded from adjusted EPS, but GAAP net income will fall sharply QoQ against Q2's inflated $1.11B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 gain was excluded from non-GAAP and did not prevent -14.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is excluded from the adjusted bar, so it only touches GAAP headlines. Its size is uncertain because the quarter-end SPCX price could not be sourced.
findings.independence: Fair value $3,007M is from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001318605/000162828026049270/tsla-20260630.htm). The SPCX price is from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/spcx/price-targets).

findings.finding: The EPS bar was cut into the print. Zacks consensus fell 3c in 30 days to ~$0.44; JPMorgan cut its estimate to $0.36 from $0.49 (against a $0.43 consensus) and flagged risk of further FY27 cuts; S&P/Visible Alpha says operating EPS estimates were lowered 19% to $0.45. Meanwhile revenue drivers (deliveries) beat, which lowers the hurdle for an adjusted-EPS beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 consensus was $0.51-0.55 and the actual $0.33, a miss that drew -14.5%. Q1 2026 drew -3.56%, Q4 2025 -3.45%, Q3 2025 +2.28%.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (aggregator page, ~23 days before capture; JPM note via Brian Sozzi/Yahoo)
findings.why_not_priced: Lower estimates are public. The point is that the bar fell while the volume input beat, a mismatch that would not exist if estimates had been refreshed after 10-02.
findings.independence: S&P Global/Visible Alpha preview (https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/10/tesla-s-revenue-earnings-expected-to-edge-lower-despite-delivery-beat, 2026-10-15) and Zacks via search.

findings.finding: Tesla guided 2026 capex above $25B, rising for another 2-3 years, with FCF negative for the rest of 2026. Q3 capex is expected around $7.94B (Visible Alpha) and H1 capex was $8.28B. A confirmation, or a raise toward 2027 AI/Optimus spending, is a near-certain call topic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capex at >$25B was reaffirmed in Q2 alongside the -14.5% reaction. Peer SpaceX fell 9% on a capex surge at its Q2 (Aug 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance, so it is sized toward 0. The residual risk is a 2027 capex number, which no source carries yet.

searched_and_found_nothing: Tesla company-compiled Q3 2026 earnings consensus on ir.tesla.com (403 on fetch; only the delivery consensus was found via secondary sources)
October 2026 NHTSA recall or investigation news (latest is the 2026-07-31 suspension probe)
News dated 10-19/10-20 explaining the +6.9% move from 362.44 to 387.38 (only Roadster-event coverage found)
Lithium carbonate price trend through Q3 2026 (rangebound in September per Mysteel headlines; no number)
Current TSLA short interest (latest found is the 2026-03-31 settlement)
Explicit Q3 margin guidance from the Q2 call

rejected_candidates.candidate: Musk's Japan Supercharger/service investment and the +4.2% day
rejected_candidates.detail: Dated 2026-03-30 (Musk confirmed it that day), so stale news, not a pre-print catalyst. The closest of the four reasons is outside_window, but strictly it is a stale event, not a future one.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Roadster reveal on 2026-10-15, production targeted for 2028
rejected_candidates.detail: Already in the price before the window (shares rose after the event). No financial content in Q3, and a 2028 product ramp has no path to this print. Filed as already-reflected context.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Gasgoo article: Tesla sold 11,329 China-made vehicles in September
rejected_candidates.detail: Does not match the 2026 CPCA figure of 95,366 wholesale; it appears to be from an earlier year.

baseline_tension: Roughly neutral against the baseline. The skew is only mildly put-bid (+1.57) and the run-up is a modest +5.5% over 5 days. Findings are near-balanced (+0.10). The name's own earnings reaction history (3 of 4 negative, -14.5% last time on a revenue beat with an EPS miss) argues against reading the delivery beat as a long, so p_up is held at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): delivery-beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because Q2's revenue beat drew -14.5%.
Lesson 1: bar-cut finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2 for the same reaction history.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): bitcoin fair-value gain cut from +0.3 to +0.15 and SpaceX mark from -0.1 to -0.05, below operating income with no path to guidance.

Lesson 9 (segments): China discount finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, net of the European registration growth filed separately; energy miss from -0.3 to -0.2, net of the non-recurring Q2 warranty charge.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked (~1.7% of shares, stale), not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
Lesson 6 (bar): adjusted EPS bar sourced from two agreeing estimates ($0.44, Zacks and Visible Alpha), so sizes are not capped.
